newsitem.title: ITALY: Visco doubts Italy will need '97 mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Visco doubts Italy will need '97 mini-budget.

text.p: Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said on Friday he doubted that the country would need additional budget cutting measures on top of its planned 1997 package.
Visco told the Senate speculation on the need for a mini-budget next year to help Italy meet economic criteria to join the proposed European single currency could prove unfounded.

In a reply session before the house moves to voting on sections of the 1997 budget package, Visco said fiscal revenues were "going very well" even though income from value added tax was 4.0 to 5.0 trillion lire below forecasts and revenue from a tax amnesty was 1.0 trillion below estimates.

"Effects of spending cuts were forecast conservatively so I am confident that the objectives can be met and that therefore the debate on the necessity of adding to the budget could be unfounded," he said.

Italian employers' association Confindustria said recently that the budget package, which aims for 62.5 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures, will not be sufficient to meet the government's targets, leaving an overshoot of 38.0 trillion.
Visco told the Senate he thought "a rebalancing of welfare" would be necessary, particularly in pensions where spending was higher than in other countries.
But he added a reduction in the deficit from one year to the next of 25.0 trillion lire via spending cuts was not possible.

The budget package is currently being examined by the upper house. Voting is supposed to start on Friday afternoon although some 3,000 amendments have been submitted to the bill, making a confidence vote more likely.
The package is scheduled to be approved by December 19 before returning for final approval in the lower house ahead of an end-year deadline.
